title: All products with their prices
question: Show all products: their code (MAHH), name (TENHH), unit price (DONGIA), and stock quantity (SLTON). Order by price descending.
hint: Use SELECT ... FROM HANG_HOA with ORDER BY

title: Products in a specific group
question: Find all products in the 'Thực phẩm' (Food) group. Show MAHH, TENHH, DONGIA. The group code for food is 'TP'.
hint: Use WHERE MANHOM = 'TP'

title: Products with group names
question: Show all products with their group name. Display MAHH, TENHH (as 'SanPham'), TENNHOM (as 'NhomHang'), and DONGIA.
solution:
SELECT h.MAHH, h.TENHH AS SanPham, n.TENNHOM AS NhomHang, h.DONGIA
FROM HANG_HOA h
JOIN NHOM_HANG n ON h.MANHOM = n.MANHOM
ORDER BY n.TENNHOM, h.MAHH;
hint: Use JOIN NHOM_HANG ON h.MANHOM = n.MANHOM

title: Products per group
question: Count how many products are in each product group. Show TENNHOM (group name) and the count (as 'SoLuong').
solution:
SELECT n.TENNHOM, COUNT(*) AS SoLuong
FROM HANG_HOA h
JOIN NHOM_HANG n ON h.MANHOM = n.MANHOM
GROUP BY n.TENNHOM;
hint: Use GROUP BY with COUNT(*)

title: Revenue by product group
question: Calculate total revenue (sum of THANHTIEN) for each product group. Show TENNHOM and total revenue (as 'DoanhThu'). Order by revenue descending.
solution:
SELECT n.TENNHOM, SUM(c.THANHTIEN) AS DoanhThu
FROM CTHD c
JOIN HANG_HOA h ON c.MAHH = h.MAHH
JOIN NHOM_HANG n ON h.MANHOM = n.MANHOM
GROUP BY n.TENNHOM
ORDER BY DoanhThu DESC;
hint: Join CTHD → HANG_HOA → NHOM_HANG, then GROUP BY

title: Top 3 best-selling products
question: Find the top 3 products by total quantity sold (SLBAN). Show MAHH, TENHH, and total quantity sold (as 'TongSL').
solution:
SELECT h.MAHH, h.TENHH, SUM(c.SLBAN) AS TongSL
FROM CTHD c
JOIN HANG_HOA h ON c.MAHH = h.MAHH
GROUP BY h.MAHH
ORDER BY TongSL DESC
LIMIT 3;
hint: Use SUM(c.SLBAN), GROUP BY, ORDER BY DESC, LIMIT 3

title: Employees grouped by role
question: For each employee type, show the role name (TENLOAI) and the number of employees (as 'SoNV'). Only include types that have at least 5 employees.
solution:
SELECT l.TENLOAI, COUNT(*) AS SoNV
FROM NHAN_VIEN e
JOIN LOAI_NV l ON e.MALNV = l.MALNV
GROUP BY l.TENLOAI
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5;
hint: Use HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5 after GROUP BY

title: Invoice details with product and agent names
question: Show invoice details: MAHD, TENHH (product name), SLBAN (quantity sold), and TENDL (agent name). Join CTHD → HANG_HOA for product and CTHD → HOA_DON → DAI_LY for agent.
solution:
SELECT c.MAHD, h.TENHH, c.SLBAN, dl.TENDL
FROM CTHD c
JOIN HANG_HOA h ON c.MAHH = h.MAHH
JOIN HOA_DON hd ON c.MAHD = hd.MAHD
JOIN DAI_LY dl ON hd.MADL = dl.MADL;
hint: You need 3 JOINs: CTHD → HANG_HOA, CTHD → HOA_DON, HOA_DON → DAI_LY

title: Products above average price
question: Find products whose price (DONGIA) is higher than the average price of all products. Show MAHH, TENHH, DONGIA.
hint: Use WHERE DONGIA > (SELECT AVG(DONGIA) FROM HANG_HOA)

title: Highest-spending agent
question: Which agent (TENDL) spent the most total money across all invoices? Show TENDL and total spent (as 'TongChiTieu'). Order by total descending, limit 1.
solution:
SELECT dl.TENDL, SUM(c.THANHTIEN) AS TongChiTieu
FROM CTHD c
JOIN HOA_DON hd ON c.MAHD = hd.MAHD
JOIN DAI_LY dl ON hd.MADL = dl.MADL
GROUP BY dl.MADL
ORDER BY TongChiTieu DESC
LIMIT 1;
hint: Use 3 JOINs, GROUP BY agent, ORDER BY SUM, LIMIT 1

title: Invoices in a date range
question: Show all invoices from February 2008. Display MAHD, NGAYLAP, TONGTIEN, and TENDL (agent name). Order by invoice code.
solution:
SELECT hd.MAHD, hd.NGAYLAP, hd.TONGTIEN, dl.TENDL
FROM HOA_DON hd
JOIN DAI_LY dl ON hd.MADL = dl.MADL
WHERE hd.NGAYLAP >= '2008-02-01' AND hd.NGAYLAP < '2008-03-01'
ORDER BY hd.MAHD;
hint: Use WHERE NGAYLAP >= '2008-02-01' AND NGAYLAP < '2008-03-01'

title: Team revenue ranking
question: Calculate total revenue generated by each team. Show MADOI (team code) and total revenue (as 'DoanhThu'). Only include teams that have generated revenue. Order by revenue descending.
solution:
SELECT e.MADOI, SUM(c.THANHTIEN) AS DoanhThu
FROM CTHD c
JOIN HOA_DON hd ON c.MAHD = hd.MAHD
JOIN NHAN_VIEN e ON hd.MANV = e.MANV
WHERE e.MADOI IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY e.MADOI
ORDER BY DoanhThu DESC;
hint: Join CTHD → HOA_DON → NHAN_VIEN, filtering out NULL teams with WHERE e.MADOI IS NOT NULL

title: Invoices with high discounts
question: Find invoice details where the discount rate (CKBAN) is 20% or more. Show MAHD, TENHH (product name), SLBAN, CKBAN, THANHTIEN, and TENDL (agent name). Order by discount descending.
solution:
SELECT c.MAHD, h.TENHH, c.SLBAN, c.CKBAN, c.THANHTIEN, dl.TENDL
FROM CTHD c
JOIN HANG_HOA h ON c.MAHH = h.MAHH
JOIN HOA_DON hd ON c.MAHD = hd.MAHD
JOIN DAI_LY dl ON hd.MADL = dl.MADL
WHERE c.CKBAN >= 0.20
ORDER BY c.CKBAN DESC;
hint: Filter with WHERE CKBAN >= 0.20

title: Distinct product groups
question: Your inventory manager wants to know how many different product groups the company sells products in. Show all distinct group codes (MANHOM) from the product catalog. This gives an overview of which product categories are active.
hint: Use the DISTINCT keyword to remove duplicate values

title: Search agents by name
question: The sales team needs a list of agents whose name contains the phrase 'bách hóa' (general store). Show the agent code (MADL), name (TENDL), and address (DIACHI).
hint: Use WHERE TENDL LIKE with % wildcards around the search term

title: Packaging without secondary unit
question: Some packaging formats have a secondary packaging level (LOC) and some don't. Show all packaging formats that do NOT have a lốc (LOC) value — meaning they only sell by the thùng (case). Display MAHTDG and THUNG.
hint: Use WHERE LOC IS NULL to find rows with no LOC value

title: Products in selected groups
question: The marketing team is running a promotion and needs all products from the 'Bột' (BOT) and 'Thực phẩm' (TP) groups. Show MAHH, TENHH, and DONGIA. Use a single WHERE clause instead of multiple OR conditions.
hint: Use IN ('BOT', 'TP') instead of multiple OR conditions

title: Price statistics
question: The finance team needs a quick overview of the product pricing. Show the cheapest price (as 'GiaThapNhat'), the most expensive price (as 'GiaCaoNhat'), and the average price (as 'GiaTrungBinh') across all products.
solution:
SELECT MIN(DONGIA) AS GiaThapNhat, MAX(DONGIA) AS GiaCaoNhat, AVG(DONGIA) AS GiaTrungBinh
FROM HANG_HOA;
hint: Use MIN(), MAX(), and AVG() aggregate functions

title: Products that have been sold
question: The warehouse manager wants to know which products have at least one sale. Show MAHH and TENHH for all products that appear in any invoice line item. Avoid listing the same product twice. Use a subquery instead of a JOIN.
hint: Use WHERE MAHH IN (SELECT DISTINCT MAHH FROM CTHD)

title: Employee invoice activity
question: The manager wants to review all employees and how many invoices each has created. Show MANV, HOTEN (employee name), and the number of invoices (as 'SoHoaDon'). Include employees who have not created any invoices. Order by invoice count ascending.
solution:
SELECT e.MANV, e.HOTEN, COUNT(hd.MAHD) AS SoHoaDon
FROM NHAN_VIEN e
LEFT JOIN HOA_DON hd ON e.MANV = hd.MANV
GROUP BY e.MANV
ORDER BY SoHoaDon ASC;
hint: Use LEFT JOIN to include employees with zero invoices

title: Products never sold
question: The product team is reviewing slow-moving inventory. Find products that have NEVER appeared in any invoice. Show MAHH and TENHH. Use NOT IN with a subquery.
hint: Use NOT IN with a subquery that selects MAHH from CTHD

title: Agents who have created invoices
question: The sales director needs a list of agents who HAVE created at least one invoice. Show MADL and TENDL. Use EXISTS with a correlated subquery.
hint: Use EXISTS with a correlated subquery referencing dl.MADL

title: Agents with no invoice activity
question: The sales director needs a list of agents who have NOT created any invoices. Show MADL and TENDL. Use NOT EXISTS with a correlated subquery.
hint: Use NOT EXISTS with a correlated subquery referencing dl.MADL

title: Monthly revenue in 2008
question: The finance team needs a monthly revenue report for 2008. Show each month (as 'Thang', format YYYY-MM) and the total invoice value (as 'DoanhThu'). Order by month. Hint: Use substr(NGAYLAP, 1, 7) to extract the year-month part of the date.
solution:
SELECT substr(NGAYLAP, 1, 7) AS Thang, SUM(TONGTIEN) AS DoanhThu
FROM HOA_DON
WHERE NGAYLAP >= '2008-01-01' AND NGAYLAP < '2009-01-01'
GROUP BY Thang
ORDER BY Thang;
hint: Use substr(NGAYLAP, 1, 7) to extract YYYY-MM and GROUP BY to aggregate

title: Above average for their group
question: Find products whose price is higher than the AVERAGE price of products in their OWN group. For example, a product in 'Bột' should be compared only to the average of 'Bột', not the overall average. Show MAHH, TENHH, MANHOM, DONGIA.
solution:
SELECT h.MAHH, h.TENHH, h.MANHOM, h.DONGIA
FROM HANG_HOA h
WHERE h.DONGIA > (
  SELECT AVG(DONGIA)
  FROM HANG_HOA
  WHERE MANHOM = h.MANHOM
);
hint: Use a correlated subquery: the inner WHERE references the outer table's MANHOM

title: Agents buying from all groups
question: Find agents who have purchased products from ALL product groups. This is a relational division problem: there should NOT exist a product group that the agent has NOT purchased from. Show MADL and TENDL. Use double NOT EXISTS.
solution:
SELECT dl.MADL, dl.TENDL
FROM DAI_LY dl
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT nh.MANHOM
  FROM NHOM_HANG nh
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM CTHD c
    JOIN HOA_DON hd ON c.MAHD = hd.MAHD
    JOIN HANG_HOA h ON c.MAHH = h.MAHH
    WHERE hd.MADL = dl.MADL
      AND h.MANHOM = nh.MANHOM
  )
);
hint: Use double NOT EXISTS: 'there is no product group that this agent has not bought from'

title: Product pairs in the same group
question: The product manager wants to see all possible pairs of products that belong to the same group for cross-promotion. Show both product names (as 'SP1' and 'SP2') and the shared group name (as 'NhomHang'). Each pair should appear only once. Use a self-join.
solution:
SELECT a.TENHH AS SP1, b.TENHH AS SP2, n.TENNHOM AS NhomHang
FROM HANG_HOA a
JOIN HANG_HOA b ON a.MANHOM = b.MANHOM AND a.MAHH < b.MAHH
JOIN NHOM_HANG n ON a.MANHOM = n.MANHOM
ORDER BY n.TENNHOM, a.TENHH;
hint: Self-join HANG_HOA on MANHOM with a.MAHH < b.MAHH to avoid duplicate pairs

title: Average revenue per employee
question: Management wants to know the average revenue generated per employee. First calculate each employee's total revenue (from invoice line items), then find the average across all employees. Show the result as 'DoanhThuTrungBinh'. Include employees with zero revenue. Use a derived table (subquery in FROM).
solution:
SELECT AVG(emp_rev) AS DoanhThuTrungBinh
FROM (
  SELECT e.MANV, COALESCE(SUM(c.THANHTIEN), 0) AS emp_rev
  FROM NHAN_VIEN e
  LEFT JOIN HOA_DON hd ON e.MANV = hd.MANV
  LEFT JOIN CTHD c ON hd.MAHD = c.MAHD
  GROUP BY e.MANV
);
hint: Use a subquery in FROM to calculate per-employee revenue first, then average the results

title: Products never sold at deep discount
question: The pricing team wants to find products that have NEVER been sold at a discount rate above 15% (CKBAN > 0.15). Show MAHH and TENHH. Use a correlated NOT EXISTS subquery.
solution:
SELECT h.MAHH, h.TENHH
FROM HANG_HOA h
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1
  FROM CTHD c
  JOIN HOA_DON hd ON c.MAHD = hd.MAHD
  WHERE c.MAHH = h.MAHH
    AND c.CKBAN > 0.15
);
hint: Use NOT EXISTS with a correlated subquery: c.MAHH = h.MAHH

title: Top agents by group coverage and spending
question: The sales VP wants to identify top-performing agents. Find agents who have purchased from more than 2 different product groups AND have total spending (sum of THANHTIEN) over 1,000,000 VND. Show MADL, TENDL, number of groups (as 'SoNhom'), and total spending (as 'TongChiTieu').
solution:
SELECT dl.MADL, dl.TENDL, COUNT(DISTINCT h.MANHOM) AS SoNhom, SUM(c.THANHTIEN) AS TongChiTieu
FROM CTHD c
JOIN HOA_DON hd ON c.MAHD = hd.MAHD
JOIN DAI_LY dl ON hd.MADL = dl.MADL
JOIN HANG_HOA h ON c.MAHH = h.MAHH
GROUP BY dl.MADL
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT h.MANHOM) > 2
   AND SUM(c.THANHTIEN) > 1000000
ORDER BY TongChiTieu DESC;
hint: Use GROUP BY agent with HAVING that has TWO conditions: group count > 2 AND total > 1000000

title: Custom invoice sorting
question: The accountant has a special request: show all invoices but with a custom sort order. Agent 'Cửa hàng tổng hợp DDC' (DL003) should appear first (they are a VIP client), followed by all other agents ordered by invoice total descending. Show MAHD, TENDL, and TONGTIEN. Use CASE in ORDER BY.
solution:
SELECT hd.MAHD, dl.TENDL, hd.TONGTIEN
FROM HOA_DON hd
JOIN DAI_LY dl ON hd.MADL = dl.MADL
ORDER BY
  CASE WHEN dl.MADL = 'DL003' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END,
  hd.TONGTIEN DESC;
hint: Use CASE in ORDER BY to assign sort priority: 0 for VIP agent (DL003), 1 for everyone else

title: Delivery notes with employee names
question: The warehouse manager wants to see all delivery notes with the employee who received each shipment. Show MAPX, NGAYXUAT, and HOTEN. Order by NGAYXUAT.
solution:
SELECT px.MAPX, px.NGAYXUAT, nv.HOTEN
FROM PHIEU_XUAT px
JOIN NHAN_VIEN nv ON px.MANV = nv.MANV
ORDER BY px.NGAYXUAT;
hint: Use JOIN PHIEU_XUAT with NHAN_VIEN ON MANV

title: Delivery note line items with product names
question: Show all delivery line items with product information. Display MAPX, MAHH, TENHH, and SOLUONG. Order by MAPX then MAHH.
solution:
SELECT c.MAPX, c.MAHH, h.TENHH, c.SOLUONG
FROM CTPX c
JOIN HANG_HOA h ON c.MAHH = h.MAHH
ORDER BY c.MAPX, c.MAHH;
hint: Use JOIN CTPX with HANG_HOA ON MAHH

title: Total quantity delivered per product
question: The warehouse team needs to know the total quantity delivered for each product. Show MAHH, TENHH, and total quantity (as TongSLXuat). Order by total descending.
solution:
SELECT c.MAHH, h.TENHH, SUM(c.SOLUONG) AS TongSLXuat
FROM CTPX c
JOIN HANG_HOA h ON c.MAHH = h.MAHH
GROUP BY c.MAHH
ORDER BY TongSLXuat DESC;
hint: Use GROUP BY with SUM and ORDER BY DESC

title: Products never delivered
question: The warehouse supervisor wants to know which products have never been requested for delivery. Show MAHH and TENHH for products that do not appear in any delivery note.
hint: Use NOT IN with a subquery selecting MAHH from CTPX

title: Products delivered more than sold
question: The supply chain director wants to compare delivery vs sales. Find products where total delivered quantity exceeds total sold quantity. Show MAHH and TENHH.
hint: Use a correlated subquery with HAVING to compare delivery and sales quantities

title: Products in deliveries or sales
question: The logistics team wants a consolidated product list. Show all distinct product codes that have appeared in either a delivery note OR an invoice. Use UNION.
solution:
SELECT MAHH FROM CTHD
UNION
SELECT MAHH FROM CTPX
ORDER BY MAHH;
hint: Use UNION between CTHD and CTPX subqueries

title: Products in both deliveries and sales
question: Find products that have been BOTH delivered from warehouse AND sold via invoices. Show MAHH. Use INTERSECT.
solution:
SELECT MAHH FROM CTHD
INTERSECT
SELECT MAHH FROM CTPX
ORDER BY MAHH;
hint: Use INTERSECT between CTHD and CTPX subqueries

title: Products delivered but never sold
question: Find products that have been delivered from warehouse but NEVER sold via invoice. Show MAHH and TENHH. Use EXCEPT to find the difference.
solution:
SELECT h.MAHH, h.TENHH
FROM HANG_HOA h
WHERE h.MAHH IN (
  SELECT MAHH FROM CTPX
  EXCEPT
  SELECT MAHH FROM CTHD
);
hint: Use EXCEPT to subtract CTHD products from CTPX products, then JOIN for names

title: Employees with sales and delivery activity
question: Find employees who have BOTH issued invoices AND received warehouse delivery notes. Show MANV and HOTEN. Use INTERSECT and a main query.
solution:
SELECT n.MANV, n.HOTEN
FROM NHAN_VIEN n
WHERE n.MANV IN (
  SELECT MANV FROM HOA_DON
  INTERSECT
  SELECT MANV FROM PHIEU_XUAT
)
ORDER BY n.MANV;
hint: Use INTERSECT to find employees in both HOA_DON and PHIEU_XUAT

title: Product price tier classification
question: Classify products into price tiers: Thap (DONGIA < 3000), Trung binh (3000-10000), and Cao (>10000). Show MAHH, TENHH, DONGIA, and the tier (as MucGia). Order by DONGIA.
solution:
SELECT MAHH, TENHH, DONGIA,
  CASE
    WHEN DONGIA < 3000 THEN 'Thap'
    WHEN DONGIA BETWEEN 3000 AND 10000 THEN 'Trung binh'
    WHEN DONGIA > 10000 THEN 'Cao'
  END AS MucGia
FROM HANG_HOA
ORDER BY DONGIA;
hint: Use CASE with WHEN ... THEN ... END to classify prices into tiers

title: Inventory status by product group
question: For each product group, show TENNHOM, total products (as TongSP), and how many products are well-stocked with SLTON >= 200 (as SoSPTonNhieu). Use SUM with CASE.
solution:
SELECT n.TENNHOM, COUNT(*) AS TongSP,
  SUM(CASE WHEN h.SLTON >= 200 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS SoSPTonNhieu
FROM HANG_HOA h
JOIN NHOM_HANG n ON h.MANHOM = n.MANHOM
GROUP BY n.TENNHOM;
hint: Use SUM(CASE WHEN ... THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) for conditional counting

title: Delivery pivot by product group
question: The warehouse manager needs to see each employee's delivery distribution across product groups. For each employee who has made deliveries, show HOTEN, and three pivot columns: SoLuongBOT, SoLuongTP, SoLuongCSTT (total items delivered from each group).
solution:
SELECT nv.HOTEN,
  SUM(CASE WHEN h.MANHOM = 'BOT' THEN c.SOLUONG ELSE 0 END) AS SoLuongBOT,
  SUM(CASE WHEN h.MANHOM = 'TP' THEN c.SOLUONG ELSE 0 END) AS SoLuongTP,
  SUM(CASE WHEN h.MANHOM = 'CSTT' THEN c.SOLUONG ELSE 0 END) AS SoLuongCSTT
FROM PHIEU_XUAT px
JOIN NHAN_VIEN nv ON px.MANV = nv.MANV
JOIN CTPX c ON px.MAPX = c.MAPX
JOIN HANG_HOA h ON c.MAHH = h.MAHH
GROUP BY nv.MANV
ORDER BY nv.HOTEN;
hint: Use CASE inside SUM for each product group to create a pivot table

title: Employees in numbered districts
question: Find employees whose address contains Q followed by a digit (indicating a numbered district). Show HOTEN and DIACHI. Use the _ wildcard to match the exact character after Q. Order by HOTEN.
solution:
SELECT HOTEN, DIACHI
FROM NHAN_VIEN
WHERE DIACHI LIKE '%Q_%'
ORDER BY HOTEN;
hint: Use LIKE with _ wildcard: %Q_% matches Q followed by any single character

title: Products with gram weight in name
question: Find products whose name ends with g (indicating weight in grams). Show MAHH and TENHH. Order by MAHH.
solution:
SELECT MAHH, TENHH
FROM HANG_HOA
WHERE TENHH LIKE '%g'
ORDER BY MAHH;
hint: Use LIKE with %g pattern to find names ending with g

title: Brand name verification by group
question: The marketing team wants to verify that product names match their assigned group. For each product, show MAHH, TENHH, TENNHOM, and a column KhopNhom with value Co if the name matches the group's known brands, otherwise Khong. Brands: BOT -> Omo/Viso, CSTT -> Close-up/Lifebouy/Clear/Dove, CSSD -> Ponds, TP -> Icetea/Chao/Bot nem.
solution:
SELECT h.MAHH, h.TENHH, n.TENNHOM,
  CASE
    WHEN (h.MANHOM = 'BOT' AND (h.TENHH LIKE '%Omo%' OR h.TENHH LIKE '%Viso%'))
      OR (h.MANHOM = 'CSTT' AND (h.TENHH LIKE '%Close-up%' OR h.TENHH LIKE '%Lifebouy%'
           OR h.TENHH LIKE '%Clear%' OR h.TENHH LIKE '%Dove%'))
      OR (h.MANHOM = 'CSSD' AND h.TENHH LIKE '%Ponds%')
      OR (h.MANHOM = 'TP' AND (h.TENHH LIKE '%Icetea%' OR h.TENHH LIKE '%Chao%'
           OR h.TENHH LIKE '%Bot nem%'))
    THEN 'Co'
    ELSE 'Khong'
  END AS KhopNhom
FROM HANG_HOA h
JOIN NHOM_HANG n ON h.MANHOM = n.MANHOM
ORDER BY h.MAHH;
hint: Use CASE with multiple LIKE conditions to check brand-group alignment

title: Employees on same team with different roles
question: Find pairs of employees who work in the same team (MADOI) but have different job roles (MALNV). Show both names (as NV1 and NV2), their roles (as VaiTro1 and VaiTro2), and the team code. Each pair should appear once. Order by team code.
solution:
SELECT a.HOTEN AS NV1, b.HOTEN AS NV2,
       a.MALNV AS VaiTro1, b.MALNV AS VaiTro2, a.MADOI
FROM NHAN_VIEN a
JOIN NHAN_VIEN b ON a.MADOI = b.MADOI AND a.MANV < b.MANV AND a.MALNV != b.MALNV
ORDER BY a.MADOI;
hint: Self-join NHAN_VIEN on MADOI with a.MANV < b.MANV and different MALNV

title: Products with nearby pricing in the same group
question: The pricing team wants to find products in the same group with similar prices (difference <= 5000 VND, positive difference). Show both product names (as SP1 and SP2), their prices, price difference (as ChenhLech), and group name. SP1 should be cheaper. Order by group and difference.
solution:
SELECT a.TENHH AS SP1, b.TENHH AS SP2,
       a.DONGIA AS Gia1, b.DONGIA AS Gia2,
       b.DONGIA - a.DONGIA AS ChenhLech, n.TENNHOM AS NhomHang
FROM HANG_HOA a
JOIN HANG_HOA b ON a.MANHOM = b.MANHOM AND a.MAHH < b.MAHH
JOIN NHOM_HANG n ON a.MANHOM = n.MANHOM
WHERE a.DONGIA < b.DONGIA AND b.DONGIA - a.DONGIA <= 5000
ORDER BY n.TENNHOM, ChenhLech;
hint: Self-join HANG_HOA on MANHOM, filter by positive price difference <= 5000

title: Team activity: delivery vs sales comparison
question: Compare team performance across two activity types. For each team, show MADOI, number of delivery notes (as SoPhieuXuat), and number of invoices (as SoHoaDon). Use COUNT DISTINCT. Include teams with zero activity. Order by team code.
solution:
SELECT d.MADOI,
  COUNT(DISTINCT px.MAPX) AS SoPhieuXuat,
  COUNT(DISTINCT hd.MAHD) AS SoHoaDon
FROM DOI d
LEFT JOIN NHAN_VIEN nv ON d.MADOI = nv.MADOI
LEFT JOIN PHIEU_XUAT px ON nv.MANV = px.MANV
LEFT JOIN HOA_DON hd ON nv.MANV = hd.MANV
GROUP BY d.MADOI
ORDER BY d.MADOI;
hint: Use LEFT JOIN through DOI -> NHAN_VIEN -> PHIEU_XUAT and HOA_DON

title: Product status: sold, delivered, both, or inactive
question: Create a product status report. Show MAHH, TENHH, and a column TrangThai with values: Da ban va xuat kho (sold AND delivered), Chi ban (only sold), Chi xuat (only delivered), Khong hoat dong (no activity). Use CASE with EXISTS.
solution:
SELECT h.MAHH, h.TENHH,
  CASE
    WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM CTHD WHERE MAHH = h.MAHH)
     AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM CTPX WHERE MAHH = h.MAHH)
      THEN 'Da ban va xuat kho'
    WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM CTHD WHERE MAHH = h.MAHH)
      THEN 'Chi ban'
    WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM CTPX WHERE MAHH = h.MAHH)
      THEN 'Chi xuat'
    ELSE 'Khong hoat dong'
  END AS TrangThai
FROM HANG_HOA h
ORDER BY h.MAHH;
hint: Use CASE with multiple EXISTS subqueries to classify each product

title: Products sold but not delivered
question: Find products that have been sold via invoice but NEVER delivered from warehouse (i.e., exist in CTHD but not in CTPX). Show MAHH. Use EXCEPT.
solution:
SELECT MAHH FROM CTHD
EXCEPT
SELECT MAHH FROM CTPX
ORDER BY MAHH;
hint: Use EXCEPT to subtract delivered products from sold products

title: All product movements (delivery and sales)
question: The warehouse needs a consolidated log of all product movements. List every product movement from both delivery notes (CTPX) and invoices (CTHD). Show MAHH, SOLUONG, and a column LOAIGIAODICH with values 'XUAT_KHO' for deliveries and 'BAN_LE' for sales. Use UNION ALL. Order by MAHH then LOAIGIAODICH.
solution:
SELECT MAHH, SOLUONG AS SOLUONG, 'XUAT_KHO' AS LOAIGIAODICH
FROM CTPX
UNION ALL
SELECT MAHH, SLBAN, 'BAN_LE'
FROM CTHD
ORDER BY MAHH, LOAIGIAODICH;
hint: Use UNION ALL with a literal label column to identify the source

title: Combined movement totals per product
question: Calculate the total quantity moved (delivered + sold) for each product. Use UNION ALL to combine CTPX.SOLUONG and CTHD.SLBAN, then GROUP BY and SUM. Show MAHH and TONG_SOLUONG. Order by TONG_SOLUONG descending.
solution:
SELECT MAHH, SUM(SOLUONG) AS TONG_SOLUONG
FROM (
    SELECT MAHH, SOLUONG FROM CTPX
    UNION ALL
    SELECT MAHH, SLBAN FROM CTHD
)
GROUP BY MAHH
ORDER BY TONG_SOLUONG DESC;
hint: Wrap UNION ALL in a subquery, then GROUP BY and aggregate

title: Products above their group's average price
question: Find products whose price (DONGIA) exceeds the average price of all products in the SAME product group. Show MAHH, TENHH, DONGIA, and MANHOM. Use a correlated subquery in WHERE. Order by group then price descending.
solution:
SELECT h.MAHH, h.TENHH, h.DONGIA, h.MANHOM
FROM HANG_HOA h
WHERE h.DONGIA > (
    SELECT AVG(h2.DONGIA)
    FROM HANG_HOA h2
    WHERE h2.MANHOM = h.MANHOM
)
ORDER BY h.MANHOM, h.DONGIA DESC;
hint: The inner WHERE clause references the outer table's MANHOM — that makes it a correlated subquery

title: Products with above-average stock in their group
question: Find products whose stock quantity (SLTON) is higher than the average stock of all products in the same group. Show MAHH, TENHH, SLTON, and MANHOM. Use a correlated subquery. Order by group then stock descending.
solution:
SELECT h.MAHH, h.TENHH, h.SLTON, h.MANHOM
FROM HANG_HOA h
WHERE h.SLTON > (
    SELECT AVG(h2.SLTON)
    FROM HANG_HOA h2
    WHERE h2.MANHOM = h.MANHOM
)
ORDER BY h.MANHOM, h.SLTON DESC;
hint: Same correlated subquery pattern as the average-price exercise, but compare SLTON instead of DONGIA

title: Invoices with more items than average
question: Find invoices that contain more distinct products than the average number of products per invoice. Show MAHD, NGAYLAP, TONGTIEN, and the number of products (as SO_MATHANG). Use a subquery in HAVING to get the average. Order by SO_MATHANG descending.
solution:
SELECT hd.MAHD, hd.NGAYLAP, hd.TONGTIEN, COUNT(ct.MAHH) AS SO_MATHANG
FROM HOA_DON hd
JOIN CTHD ct ON hd.MAHD = ct.MAHD
GROUP BY hd.MAHD
HAVING COUNT(ct.MAHH) > (
    SELECT AVG(item_count) FROM (
        SELECT COUNT(ct2.MAHH) AS item_count
        FROM HOA_DON hd2
        JOIN CTHD ct2 ON hd2.MAHD = ct2.MAHD
        GROUP BY hd2.MAHD
    )
)
ORDER BY SO_MATHANG DESC;
hint: Use a subquery in HAVING with a nested subquery to compute the average item count

title: Least expensive product in each group
question: Find the cheapest product in each product group. Show group name (TENNHOM), product code (MAHH), product name (TENHH), and its price (DONGIA). Use a correlated subquery with MIN to find the minimum price per group. Order by group name.
solution:
SELECT nh.TENNHOM, h.MAHH, h.TENHH, h.DONGIA
FROM HANG_HOA h
JOIN NHOM_HANG nh ON h.MANHOM = nh.MANHOM
WHERE h.DONGIA = (
    SELECT MIN(h2.DONGIA)
    FROM HANG_HOA h2
    WHERE h2.MANHOM = h.MANHOM
)
ORDER BY nh.TENNHOM;
hint: Use a correlated subquery with MIN() to find the lowest price within each group, then match products with that exact price

title: Products delivered by every team in their group
question: Find products that have been delivered by EVERY team responsible for their product group. Use double NOT EXISTS — there should NOT exist a team covering the product's group that has NOT delivered that product. Show MAHH, TENHH, and MANHOM. Order by MAHH.
solution:
SELECT h.MAHH, h.TENHH, h.MANHOM
FROM HANG_HOA h
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT d.MADOI
    FROM DOI d
    WHERE d.MANHOM = h.MANHOM
    AND NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
        FROM PHIEU_XUAT px
        JOIN CTPX ct ON px.MAPX = ct.MAPX
        JOIN NHAN_VIEN nv ON px.MANV = nv.MANV
        WHERE nv.MADOI = d.MADOI AND ct.MAHH = h.MAHH
    )
)
ORDER BY h.MAHH;
hint: Double NOT EXISTS is the relational division pattern: for each team, check there is no missing delivery

title: Employees who sell but never receive delivery
question: Find employees who have issued invoices but NEVER received any warehouse delivery note. Show MANV and HOTEN. Use EXCEPT inside IN to subtract employees with delivery notes from employees with invoices. Order by MANV.
solution:
SELECT nv.MANV, nv.HOTEN
FROM NHAN_VIEN nv
WHERE nv.MANV IN (
    SELECT MANV FROM HOA_DON
    EXCEPT
    SELECT MANV FROM PHIEU_XUAT
)
ORDER BY nv.MANV;
hint: Combine EXCEPT with IN: first find employees in invoices, then subtract those in delivery notes

title: Employees grouped by activity type
question: List all employees involved in at least one business activity, with a label showing whether they handle sales or delivery. Use UNION to combine two sets: employees with invoices (label 'CO_HOA_DON') and employees with delivery notes (label 'CO_PHIEU_XUAT'). Show MANV, HOTEN, and VAITRO. Order by MANV then VAITRO.
solution:
SELECT nv.MANV, nv.HOTEN, 'CO_HOA_DON' AS VAITRO
FROM NHAN_VIEN nv
WHERE nv.MANV IN (SELECT MANV FROM HOA_DON)
UNION
SELECT nv.MANV, nv.HOTEN, 'CO_PHIEU_XUAT'
FROM NHAN_VIEN nv
WHERE nv.MANV IN (SELECT MANV FROM PHIEU_XUAT)
ORDER BY MANV, VAITRO;
hint: Each SELECT creates one set; UNION combines them; the literal label column identifies the source
